newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland sugar industry at standstill-union.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland sugar industry at standstill-union.

text.p: Sugar mills in north Queensland have shut down as 6000 workers obeyed union calls for a 24-hour strike, an Australian Workers Union (AWU) official said.
The strike against new state government workers compensation legislation showed "sugar workers were as concerned as any other industry," AWU offical Damien Green told Reuters.
Green said he agreed with statements by AWU Far-North Queensland organiser Darryl Noack that the strike was aimed at "sending a message to the (state) government."
Green said 24 mills were now inactive after workers from the AWU, Communications Electrical and Plumbing union and the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union walked off at midnight last night.
Earlier CANEGROWERS chairman Harry Bonanno said growers could lose between A$500,000 and A$1 million as this year's record crush could be pushed into the wet season because of the 24-hour strike.
Recent fine weather had seen about 1.8 million tonnes of cane harvested each week for the past three weeks.
The sugar industry unions held the stoppage despite a recommendation on Monday by the Queensland Industrial Relations Comission that employees remain at work.
